10.0.0.en: After a contrite prayer filled with tears and humility before God, accompanied by fasting, Ezra sensed that the prayer had been answered, for those around him were moved when they heard his prayer and told others of the people. A great number of the people gathered, men, women and children, and stood behind him before the house of the Lord, praying and weeping as he did, confessing their sins and offering repentance with contrition.

10.0.1.en: Ezra resembles Moses and Paul in their intercession for their peoples before God (Ex 32:33; 2 Cor 11:29), and he is even a type of Christ, who prayed in the Garden of Gethsemane and was crucified for us, to intercede for us by His blood with an intercession of atonement that removes all our sins. That is, the supplicating intercession of Ezra, Moses and Paul is great in the eyes of God, that He may extend His mercies to us and forgive our sins in the blood of Christ.

10.0.2.en: Ezra prayed with all his heart, his garments torn and his tears pouring down, and he took no thought of his position. He was an example of deep, repentant prayer before his people, so that a huge crowd gathered and shared in his prayer and tears. It is understood from this that Ezra's prayer was long, and that during it this great people gathered, and part of this prayer was recorded in the previous chapter (ch. 9:6-15).

10.1.0.en: Shechaniah is a Hebrew word meaning "God dwells", and he was a man in whose heart God truly dwelt, and he was deeply moved by Ezra's prayer. If Jehiel his father is the one mentioned in (v. 26), then Shechaniah suffered from the problem of pagan marriages in the form of his father's pagan wife. He came forward before Ezra and the whole assembly of the people, declaring his confession of the unfaithfulness of the people, although he himself had not married a foreign woman, but he followed the example of Ezra, who confessed on behalf of his people.

10.1.1.en: A great virtue appears in Shechaniah, namely hope in God, who does not forsake His people but forgives them if they repent and obey His commandments by putting away the foreign marriages. He was not content with being moved and weeping, like the rest of the people, but came forward with a confession like Ezra's, and then with promises that we will see in the following two verses. Shechaniah here represents the people who support their leader Ezra with repentance, confession and hope, as the Church does when she prays in the Liturgy for the Pope, the bishops, the priests and the deacons.

10.1.2.en: If the unfaithfulness of one person, Achan the son of Carmi, caused defeat for all the people of God in the days of Joshua the son of Nun (Josh 7), then when unfaithfulness spreads among the people through marriage to pagan women, it requires collective repentance from the people and separation from evil, that God may have mercy and forgive.

10.2.0.en: The repentance of Shechaniah, as a representative of the people, was joined to action, so he declared the people's readiness to separate from the pagan wives and send them away with their children, that is, to cut off sin and everything connected with it; for they were the source of the evil into which they cast their husbands, in the worship of idols and all the customs of the pagans contrary to the commandments of God. This act was not cruelty on the part of Shechaniah, because the causes of evil, namely the pagan wives, must be removed; besides, if these wives loved their husbands, they had come to believe in God and worship Him and had circumcised their male children, and therefore they would not be exposed to being sent away. Especially since these marriages were not lawful and did not need a divorce, but were relationships of adultery whose only cause was lust, as is proved by his saying "put away all the wives" and not "the wives", for no marriage contract had been made for them, and therefore they did not need a bill of divorce. We see Shechaniah's submission to the Law in his saying "according to the law", and his humility in his saying "according to the counsel of my lord", that is, Ezra.

10.2.1.en: Here Shechaniah affirms the support of the people, who fear God, for Ezra, and he asks him, with the help of God, to cleanse the people of the pagan women, for God loves him and for his sake His people will see them.

10.2.2.en: Shechaniah asked Ezra to carry out the will of God by saying "for this matter belongeth unto thee", that is, carry out the Law of God to separate the people from evil.

10.2.3.en: Shechaniah was convinced of the gravity of marrying pagan women, but it was not within his authority to separate the people from them, so he looked to Ezra, who had the authority, and encouraged him to carry out the Law of God. Shechaniah was not content with weeping behind Ezra, like the rest of the people, but confessed the sin of the people and encouraged Ezra. For the people need a leader to lead them in the way of God, and the leader also needs the encouragement and support of the people. We see this in the rite of the Church in the Liturgy, how the people pray for the Pope and the bishops, that is, the spiritual leaders.

10.3.0.en: Ezra was indeed encouraged by the words of Shechaniah, so he arose and called the chief priests and the Levites and made them swear, they and all the people standing behind them, to carry out the Law of God by each one separating from his pagan wife and the children born of her, and they all agreed and swore to carry out the Law of God. Ezra took care that the decision to put away the pagan marriages should be a collective decision, so that all would be responsible for carrying it out, and thus he would ensure precision in the execution. He took special care over those responsible for the religious life of the people, the priests and the Levites, because they were the ones who would carry out this Law of God.

10.4.0.en: Ezra had been fasting all day, praying and weeping. After the people and their religious leaders agreed to put away the pagan marriages, Ezra arose and entered one of the chambers attached to the Temple, which was the room of a person called Johanan the son of Eliashib, who may have been one of the chief priests, or a priest, and there he completed his prayers, for he was not content with the agreement of the people to obey the Law. But he prayed that the carrying out of this Law might be completed, and afterward he ate food and rested, and most likely spent the night there, as one of the translations of the Bible states. Ezra represents the spiritual leader who does not cease from prayer and weeping before God for his people because of their faults, until these faults are completely removed; for it is mentioned that he mourned because of the unfaithfulness of those of the captivity.

10.5.0.en: The chief priests sent out a proclamation in every place where the tribe of Judah and those returning with it from the tribes of Israel lived, that they should come within three days to Jerusalem before the temple of God.

10.5.1.en: Although Ezra had authority to command the gathering of the people, since the king had given him this authority (ch. 7:26), he had the chief priests gather the people, so that the people would feel that the decision was from the whole community and not from one individual, and no one would try to resist the proclamation.

10.5.2.en: The proclamation was bound to a penalty for whoever did not come to Jerusalem, and this penalty was:

10.5.3.en: 1- That all the property of this offender be forfeited, that is, his land and possessions be taken, which he would squander and give to his pagan wife, although they were the inheritance of God for His people.

10.5.4.en: 2- He would be separated, that is, excluded and cut off from the people of God, because he was against the Law of God, so that he would feel that he was defying God, and so fear and obey the proclamation. Separation means being deprived of all the promises of God.

10.5.5.en: The proclamation gave a delay of three days, because it was a sufficient period for anyone, however far from Jerusalem he lived, to come and appear before the temple of God.

10.5.6.en: The number three signifies the Resurrection of Christ, for within this period all come to the temple of God, to declare and separate themselves from evil, so that they may rise from their lusts and live in purity before God.

10.5.7.en: Your pouring yourself out before God in fervent prayer solves all your problems, however intractable they may seem. Hold fast to prayer and be persistent with God until He restores your peace and delivers you from all evil.

10.6.s.en: (2) The promise to leave the pagan wives

10.6.0.en: The people obeyed the chief priests and came within the three days to Jerusalem, namely the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, since they were the majority, and with them of course all those returning from the captivity from the other tribes. They gathered in a square beside the Temple, most likely the square beside the Water Gate, where the people later gathered in the days of Nehemiah (Neh 8:1). The time of their gathering was in the ninth month, that is, the month of Kislev, which corresponds to the month of December, on the twentieth day of it, and this month has abundant rains, so when they gathered in the square the rain fell heavily.

10.6.1.en: The people were afraid of God because of their sin, which exposed them to the divine wrath, and because they were about to leave their pagan wives and their children by them. All this made them tremble, in addition to their shivering from the cold of the weather and the falling of the rain, so it was a fearful assembly before God, as they awaited God's judgment upon them at the hand of His priests.

10.6.2.en: We see the response of the priests and the people to the Law of God in their immediate carrying out of the words of Ezra, after they had sworn before him to carry out the Law, and they did not postpone the proclamation because of the unsuitable weather. The people obeyed and came in the midst of the rain, because of their fear of God, who is able to destroy them on account of their sin of marrying pagan women.

10.6.3.en: The people felt that heaven was expressing the wrath of God by sending down the rain, and this increased their fear and established the spirit of repentance within them.
